hints: Look at the starting material first. Ethene has a C=C double bond rich in electrons, so think about what type of addition it prefers.
Now focus on the C-Br bonds in both products. Remember that hydrolysis with aqueous NaOH replaces C-Br with C-OH.
Count how many Br atoms each product must replace, then see what final diol you get in each case and check who can actually hydrogen bond to water.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

Great start, let's look at ethene. Its pi bond is an electron rich region, so it attracts electrophiles, not nucleophiles.

Reaction type:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{electrophilic addition}$$

**Explain the two products**

In aqueous bromine, the bromonium ion intermediate can be attacked by either $\text{Br}^-$ or $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. That is why we get two addition products.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{BrCH}_2\text{Br}$$
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{BrCH}_2\text{OH} + \text{HBr}$$

**Check hydrolysis to the same compound**

Hydrolysis replaces C-Br with C-OH using aqueous NaOH and heating. Let's apply it to both.

$$\text{CH}_2\text{BrCH}_2\text{Br} + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{OHCH}_2\text{OH} + 2\text{Br}^-$$
$$\text{CH}_2\text{BrCH}_2\text{OH} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{OHCH}_2\text{OH} + \text{Br}^-$$
Both give ethane-1,2-diol, the same organic compound.

**Check hydrogen bonding**

To form hydrogen bonds with water as a donor, a molecule needs H attached directly to O, N or F. Only $\text{CH}_2\text{BrCH}_2\text{OH}$ has an O-H group, while $\text{CH}_2\text{BrCH}_2\text{Br}$ has no O-H and C-Br cannot hydrogen bond effectively.

options.A: Incorrect. No substitution has occurred here. Ethene has no leaving group to substitute, the pi bond is broken and two new groups add across the double bond, so this is addition, not nucleophilic substitution.
options.B: Incorrect. The word addition is right but nucleophilic is wrong. Alkenes undergo electrophilic addition because the pi electrons attack the electrophile $Br_2$, forming a bromonium ion which is then attacked by a nucleophile.
options.C: Correct. Both C-Br bonds can be hydrolysed to C-OH. The dibromoalkane needs two hydrolyses and the bromohydrin needs one, but both finish at ethane-1,2-diol, $CH_2OHCH_2OH$.
options.D: Incorrect. Only $CH_2BrCH_2OH$ can hydrogen bond to water because it has an O-H group to donate. $CH_2BrCH_2Br$ has only C-H and C-Br bonds, and Br is too large and not electronegative enough to form effective hydrogen bonds with water.
